name: Infantry_Claude
author: Infantry AI
description: The Claude Code harness (HARNESS H7b-2/3): launches claude (by default the interactive CLI in a terminal; headless: -p stream-json, or the persistent --input-format stream-json), reads its event stream, maps tool approval to permission modes, routes its tool calls through the watched runner, lists its models, and reads its session store and plan limits. Setting harness.claude.liveIdleMinutes ( default 0 = never): minutes a resting live claude process may idle before it is stopped; each live process holds about 150-400 MB of RAM while it exists, so lower it to reclaim memory from sessions nobody wakes (the next wake resumes). Setting harness.claude.mode (default interactive): interactive runs the interactive claude in a pseudo-terminal (ConPTY on Windows) and reads its session transcript, so requests are the CLI's own (labelled cli); headless runs claude -p stream-json (the SDK path, labelled sdk-cli) and is used only when set explicitly. Interactive mode answers the CLI's folder trust question for the session's worktree, always passes --strict-mcp-config (so a project .mcp.json is not loaded and its approval dialog never shows), and a one-shot run (keep-alive 0) has no watch hook in it. Tool approval: deny runs claude with --permission-mode dontAsk; in every mode but allowAll an interactive claude answers its permission dialogs through a PermissionRequest hook (deny; ask relays the call to the owner), and a dialog no hook answered is answered No, so a turn never hangs on it. Setting harness.claude.approvalHookSeconds (default 1800): how long claude waits for that answer.

fields.label: Stop a resting live claude after (minutes, 0 = never)
Mode: interactive (default, the Claude Code CLI as a person runs it) or headless (SDK stream-json, claude -p)
Seconds claude waits for a tool approval answer (ask mode waits for the owner); past it the dialog is answered No
